program_overview.title: Java Programming Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The language enterprises run on and placements test: core Java to real depth, then Spring Boot the way backend teams actually use it.
program_overview.description:
Java is still the backbone of enterprise software and the single most-tested language in Indian placements, and the difference between knowing Java syntax and owning Java depth, collections, concurrency, the memory model, decides both interviews and real work. This live online masterclass builds that depth in order: core Java and object-oriented thinking done properly, then the engine room, collections in depth, exceptions, multithreading and modern Java features, design patterns and JDBC with real testing habits, then the job stack: Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA, security, REST APIs designed and tested like a professional. A finale month ships a Spring Boot capstone and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: Placement-grade core: collections, concurrency and OOP at the depth interviews probe
Modern Java throughout: streams, lambdas and current LTS features, not textbook Java
Spring Boot as teams use it: REST APIs, JPA, security and tests, not hello-world
Design patterns and JDBC before the framework, so Spring is understood, not incanted
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

phase_1_foundation.title: PHASE 1: Foundation & Core Java Skills (Months 1-3, Weeks 1-13)
phase_1_foundation.description: Build rock-solid Java fundamentals. Learn programming logic, master Java syntax, OOP principles, and create your first applications.

week_1.title: Introduction to Java & Development Environment Setup
topics: What is Java? History, features, and platform independence
Java ecosystem: JDK, JRE, JVM explained
Java applications: Desktop, Web, Mobile (Android), Enterprise
Setting up development environment: IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, VS Code
Your first Java program: Hello World
Java program structure: class, main method
Java coding conventions and naming standards
projects: Hello World variations with personalized messages
week_1.practice: Daily: 30 min Java syntax practice, write 5-10 simple programs

week_2_3.title: Variables, Data Types & Operators
topics: Primitive data types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean
Wrapper classes: Integer, Double, Character, Boolean, etc.
Literals: integer, floating-point, character, string, boolean
projects: Area and perimeter calculator for shapes
week_2_3.practice: Solve 30 problems on variables, data types, and operators

week_4_5.title: Control Flow Statements
projects: Number guessing game with attempts limit
week_4_5.practice: Solve 40 control flow and loop problems

week_6_7.title: Methods & Arrays
topics: Method declaration: return type, name, parameters
Method overloading: same name, different parameters
Variable scope: local vs instance vs class
Recursion: base case and recursive case
Iterating arrays: for loop, enhanced for loop
projects: Array statistics calculator (sum, average, min, max)
Linear search and binary search implementation
Sorting algorithms: bubble sort, selection sort
week_6_7.practice: Create 25 methods for various functionalities, solve 30 array problems

week_8_9.title: Classes, Objects & OOP Basics
topics: Access modifiers: private, public, protected, default
Getters and setters (accessor and mutator methods)
projects: Student class with attributes and methods
Car class with properties and behaviors
week_8_9.practice: Create 20 different classes modeling real-world entities

week_10_11.title: Inheritance & Polymorphism
topics: super keyword: accessing parent class members
Types of inheritance: single, multilevel, hierarchical
Final keyword: final variables, methods, classes
projects: Bank account types (Account -> Savings, Current, Fixed)
Payment system with different payment types
week_10_11.practice: Build 15 inheritance hierarchies, solve 25 polymorphism problems

week_12_13.title: Abstraction & Interfaces
projects: PHASE 1 MINI CAPSTONE: Library Management System (Console-based)
Features: Books, members, issue/return, search, OOP principles
week_12_13.assessment: Phase 1 exam: a practical build defended live, plus a written paper mixing this phase with everything before it

phase_2_frontend_mastery.title: PHASE 2: Intermediate Java & Advanced Concepts (Months 4-6, Weeks 14-26)
phase_2_frontend_mastery.description: Master advanced Java features, Collections Framework, exception handling, file I/O, multithreading, and design patterns.

week_14.title: String Handling & Regular Expressions

String methods: length, charAt, substring, indexOf
String manipulation: concat, replace, trim, split
Regex patterns: character classes, quantifiers, groups
Common regex operations: validation, search, replace
Regex for email, phone, URL validation
projects: Text analyzer (word count, character count, frequency)

week_15.title: Exception Handling & Error Management

Catch block order: specific to general

week_16.title: Collections Framework - Part 1

TreeSet: sorted set using Red-Black tree

week_17.title: Collections Framework - Part 2

week_18.title: Generics & Advanced Collections
topics: Time and space complexity of operations

month_5.title: Month 5: File I/O, Multithreading & Modern Java

week_19.title: File I/O & Serialization

Creating, deleting, renaming files and directories

week_20.title: Multithreading & Concurrency - Part 1

faqs.question: What does this Java course cover?
faqs.answer: Core Java to real depth first: object-oriented programming, collections, generics, exceptions, multithreading and modern Java features, plus design patterns, JDBC and JUnit testing. Then the job stack: Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA with Hibernate, Spring Security, REST API design and testing, and production habits like deployment, monitoring and logging. A finale month ships a Spring Boot capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn Java properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Is Java still worth learning in 2026?
faqs.answer: Emphatically: banking, e-commerce, telecom and most of enterprise India run on Java, placements test it more than any other language, and modern Java (current LTS releases, streams, records, virtual threads) is a far better language than its reputation. Python took the headlines; Java kept the backends.

faqs.question: Java or Python first for placements?
faqs.answer: Either works for DSA rounds, but Java pays twice: the same language covers your DSA practice and the Spring Boot backend skills that service and product companies actually hire for. If your target is backend or enterprise roles, Java first is the efficient road; our Python courses cover the data and automation roads.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 learners. A mini batch of 3-4 learners is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International learners pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.
